interpretation: The global six-face phase and the local relative-complex-orientation phase are the same native C2 symmetry character viewed globally and locally.
keeper: The global phase and the local complex-orientation phase are one native symmetry bit seen at two scales.
next_target: native equivariant lift of the shared C2 phase character into the local U(2) complex doublet

proof.step_1: The global 64-state field is the product of the six local binary relative-complex-orientation order parameters.
proof.step_2: For g in Stab(f) intersect ker(chi_deck), g fixes the selected global phase and fixes face f, hence preserves the local binary phase at f.
proof.step_3: Therefore Stab(f) intersect ker(chi_deck) is contained in the native preimage of ker(delta_f).
proof.step_4: ker(chi_deck) has order 240 and is transitive on six faces, so its face stabilizer has order 40.
proof.step_5: The native preimage of ker(delta_f) also has order 40.
proof.step_6: Finite inclusion plus equal order forces equality of the two kernels.
proof.step_7: Both restricted chi_deck and delta_f are nontrivial C2 characters on the order-80 face stabilizer; equal kernels therefore force equal characters.

theorem: For every native face f, delta_f equals chi_deck restricted to Stab(f).
